scenes.visual: Title: Three Routes to New Genes. Show free DNA, a contacting cell pair and a phage around a recipient. Keep the existing concept colours.

scenes.tts: Bacteria can inherit genes from other bacteria. DNA arrives by three routes. Transformation takes up free DNA from the surroundings. Conjugation passes DNA through cell contact. Transduction brings DNA inside a phage, a virus that infects bacteria. This exchange gives bacteria new genes, even without meiosis. It also lets geneticists map genes by watching what enters a cell, and which genes travel together.

scenes.visual: Introduce the three routes in separate labelled panels: free DNA uptake, donor-to-recipient contact, and a phage carrying host DNA. Highlight the acquired gene in the recipient. End on gene order and linked markers as the purpose of mapping.

scenes.tts: In E coli, F is a small DNA circle. When F transfers itself, an F minus recipient becomes F plus. Chromosomal genes move only rarely. But F can join the chromosome. That donor is called H F R. Transfer now pulls chromosomal genes across in a fixed order. Pairs usually break before all of F arrives, so recipients rarely become F plus.

scenes.visual: Contrast autonomous F transfer, changing an F− recipient to F+, with integrated F in an Hfr donor transferring ordered chromosome markers. Break the Hfr pair before the trailing F sequence arrives; retain the F− label on that recipient.

scenes.tts: Phages move host genes too. In generalized transduction, a phage sometimes packs a host chromosome fragment instead of its own DNA. Any part can be carried. In specialized transduction, lambda leaves its chromosome attachment site inaccurately and takes a neighbouring gene. Only genes beside that site can move this way.

scenes.tts: Delivery and stable inheritance are different steps. A linear donor fragment must recombine into the matching stretch of the recipient chromosome to be inherited stably. On a circular chromosome, that takes an even number of crossovers, at least two, one on each side.

scenes.visual: Show arrival of a separate linear donor fragment, then two crossovers flanking the matching recipient segment. Replace that segment with donor DNA in the circle. Distinguish this chromosome-fragment model from autonomous F replication.

scenes.tts: Selection makes rare recombinants visible. Only cells with every selected ability grow. Interrupted mating uses this readout. Break H F R pairs apart at set times and score which donor genes the recipients inherited. A colony reports both entry and integration.

scenes.visual: Use selective growth to reveal rare recombinant colonies. Then show Hfr mating pairs interrupted at successive times, followed by recipient scoring. Label the colony readout as entry plus integration.

scenes.tts: Markers A, B, C and D first appear at eight, fourteen, twenty and thirty one minutes. With steady transfer, their gaps are six, six and eleven minutes. The gaps are the map.
scenes.narration: Markers a, b, c and d first appear at 8, 14, 20 and 31 minutes. With steady transfer, their gaps are 6, 6 and 11 minutes. The gaps are the map.

scenes.visual: Reuse the first worked timing axis, a at 8, b at 14, c at 20 and d at 31 minutes. Reveal adjacent gaps 6, 6 and 11, then the corresponding gene map. Display the steady-transfer assumption.

scenes.tts: Another H F R strain reads the same map backwards. Different origins and orientations give overlapping orders that close into a circle.
scenes.narration: Another Hfr strain reads the same map backwards. Different origins and orientations give overlapping orders that close into a circle.

scenes.visual: Reuse the reverse-order comparison, aligning d-c-b-a with a-b-c-d. Show matching intervals, different origins and opposite arrows, then extend overlapping orders into a circular chromosome map.

scenes.tts: Phage transfer gives a finer map. Genes carried together in a single particle must be close. Closer genes travel together more often. These frequencies compare distances, but ordering genes needs three-factor counts.

scenes.visual: Move from the circular chromosome overview to a magnified region within one P1 fragment. Compare a close marker pair with a more distant pair and their relative cotransduction frequencies. Finish with the limit: two-factor frequencies compare proximity; three-factor counts determine order.
End card: Transformation — free DNA; Conjugation — contact; Transduction — phage. Beneath, show delivery → integration for a linear chromosome fragment, and gene transfer → genetic maps.
